answer: In a degree-normalized attestation graph, trust propagates through random walks capped at \(k\) steps, limiting how far endorsements can spread. A sybil cluster can mirror legitimate identities and densely link them internally, yet a sparse external cut gives it low conductance—the outgoing edge weight relative to cluster volume. Under bounded-degree voting and min-cut/transitivity bounds, this bottleneck limits trust entering the cluster and thus its aggregate voting weight; pigment on a jetty may alter its appearance, not its connections.
